name: Setaman

sources.citation: SIL-PNG 'PNG Language Resources: Setaman' language page, Publications Online list and full PNG Bibliography list for code stm (www-01.sil.org/pacific/png/), Internet Archive copy 2015-07-24.

sources.note: Bibliographic check only: the full SIL-PNG bibliography (published + unpublished mss) for Setaman lists only Spencer & Van Cott 2010. No OPD, phonology essentials or grammar ms.

sources.citation: SIL International, Language & Culture Archives listing for Setaman [stm] (www.sil.org/resources/search/language/stm), Internet Archive copy 2015-09-19.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic check only: exactly one item for stm (archives/9006 = the 2010 survey). No Organised Phonology Data or phonology ms. exists for Setaman in the SIL archive listing.

sources.citation: Van Cott, Sara & Juliann Spencer. 2010. A Sociolinguistic Survey of Setaman [stm]. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2010-022 (June 2010). Dallas: SIL International. 57 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Appendix A 'Characteristics of the language' (pp. 35-36) gives observed consonant and vowel phone charts only and states: 'Although no phonological analysis has been performed on the Setaman wordlist data, Healey (1963) provides generalizations about Ok family languages, which may be true of Setaman as well.' A.3 relays Healey (1963:2) family-level features incl. 'contrastive accent (usually tonal) on each syllable' and adds 'These features may be present in Setaman; however, they were not observed during the analysis of the wordlist data from Setaman.' Wordlists in App. E carry no stress or…

sources.citation: Healey, Alan. 1964. The Ok language family in New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University (hdl 1885/10871).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Names 'Setaman' once, as a member of Mountain-Ok Division A (ch. II intro, p. ~37); contains no Setaman data or abbreviation. Family-level only (ch. II sec. 2.3, pp. 58-61): 'All of the Mountain-Ok languages which have been adequately examined have been found to have lexical pitch. This pitch is contrastive on each syllable of a word, with the occasional exception of the first syllable.' Section 7.3 Stress concerns Telefol only.
